author: Angela George
title: Erickson's 2-point lead sends mayoral race against Smith to a recount - NewsBreak
text:
By Angela George Gabriel Brito ,
21 hours ago First a runoff, now a recount.
After a classic cliffhanger in an already “exhausting” race, the Sioux Falls mayoral runoff election was within two votes.
Turns out every single vote counts after all.
As of midnight Tuesday night, and all 79 precincts reporting, the City of Sioux Falls unofficially called 18,279 votes for Christine Erickson and 18,277 votes for Jamie Smith, tying up the race at 49.1%.
“This is not over,” Smith said to his supporters at the Falls Overlook Café during his watch party Tuesday night. “We are not conceding until there is a recount.”
At Jack Rose Social Club, Christine Erickson told her supporters to “stay tuned.”
“We know there will be a recount, but let’s hold true to these numbers and celebrate tonight,” she said.
Round three in the ring: Now what? According to state guidelines , if a voter in a local election can only select one candidate (Erickson or Smith), then the vote margin “must not exceed 2% of the total votes cast.”
Thus, the election must be within 100 votes to automatically commence a recount.
According to the South Dakota Secretary of State's website, the recount board must consist of two Republicans, two Democrats and one recount referee. The county auditor provides administrative support to the recount board.
Until then, the Sioux Falls City Council is expected to still go through with canvassing the votes, ensuring all ballots cast are accurately counted and included in final results.
Auditors have no more than 10 days to complete a recount.
Did absentee voting predict the night? Voter turnout was the real wildcard of the night.
Like absentee voting for the runoff, the number of ballots that came in on June 23 nearly matched initial election turnout for the June 2 primary, which brought in 38,733 ballots.
According to previous reporting, 4,049 absentee ballots were cast for this runoff, nearly matching the 4,345 absentee ballots from the June 2 election, despite the runoff being a standalone race with a much shorter window (absentee voting began June 16).
On June 23, Smith took 2,333 absentee votes; Erickson had 1,862.
In total, 36,556 ballots were cast for the mayoral runoff.
Check out our live blog: Here's how Election Day has turned out.
How did we get to a runoff? For this first-ever consolidated state primary earlier this month, the five-candidate race resulted in Erickson, a Republican and former state representative, and Smith, a Democratic state senator, moving forward. Erickson had 37% or 14,407 of the votes, while Smith had 28% or 10,959 votes.
Other former opponents were former city councilor Greg Jamison, who finished with 18%; former Downtown Sioux Falls CEO Joe Batcheller, who had 15%; and political analyst David Zokaites, who had 2%.
Because city ordinance states one candidate must receive at least 51% of the vote, a runoff was scheduled for June 23.
Story continues below.
A ‘pretty R-vs-D’ endorsement race The three-week-long runoff was costly and competitive, a nonpartisan race ultimately breaking down along party lines.
After Jamison, an elected Republican, and Batchellor, an independent, endorsed Smith two days after the first election, many other runoff endorsements followed.
“It really says something when the folks you were running against embrace you like that,” Smith said Tuesday night. “It was really humbling, and I felt a real collaborative spirit.”
The start of GOP endorsements for Erickson was from gubernatorial candidates Gov. Larry Rhoden and Aberdeen businessman Toby Doeden. Then came South Dakota Attorney General Marty Jackley for Erickson, the Lincoln County sheriff and local law enforcement as well.
Other recent endorsements for Smith included Democratic State Sen. Liz Larson, former South Dakota House Rep. Linda Duba, former Sioux Falls School Board President Kent Alberty, and former Sanford Health president and CEO for the Sioux Falls region Paul Hanson.
The checks were contentious as well. After Erickson received a $100,000 PAC donation from Driving South Dakota, her supporters reminded Smith of his $10,000 endorsement from the South Dakota Democratic Party last year. Erickson also received $10,000 from the Republican party. Each received contributions from the SD RPAC.
“This election is about serving the people,” Smith said, “not serving political parties.”
Erickson, too, pushed back on the partisan narrative, despite her campaign drawing the most explicit partisan endorsement within the final stretch.
You don't need “a politician telling you how to vote,” she said last week.
In total, Erickson raised about $345,000 and Smith about $170,000, campaign finance reports show.
Angela George has covered the mayoral election for the Argus Leader in Sioux Falls, South Dakota. Email ageorge@usatodayco.com.
